- When sentiment is low (≤0.2) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot — cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak.  
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.3) and forecast is below recent mean, adjust upward by 2–5% to capture momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, if last 3–5 days show strong mean reversion, forecast should be slightly below recent high.  
- If sentiment is volatile (fluctuating 0.1–0.4) and forecast is erratic, smooth transitions by averaging 2–3 prior values.  
- When sentiment is near zero and price is trending down, forecast should not dip below 10% below recent low.
